questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The trade fair held annually at 'Ukaz in pre-Islamic Arabia was chiefly important as a venue for
options: the drafting of peace treaties with Persia
poetry recitals and tribal commerce
the collection of Islamic alms
the coronation of Arab kings
questions.explanation: The 'Ukaz fair was a famous pre-Islamic marketplace where tribes traded goods and poets competed to have their verses celebrated and displayed.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: In pre-Islamic Arabia, disputes between tribes were most commonly settled through
options: a written constitution enforced by a central king
compulsory mediation by Byzantine officials
retaliation (blood feuds) or the arbitration of a respected chief
referral to a standing Arabian supreme court
questions.explanation: In the absence of a central government, pre-Islamic Arab tribes typically resolved disputes through blood feuds or the informal arbitration of respected elders and chiefs.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The custodianship (Siqayah) of providing water to pilgrims visiting the Ka'bah before Islam was a privilege held by the clan of
options: Banu Umayyah
Banu Hashim
Banu Zuhrah
Banu Makhzum
questions.explanation: The Prophet's own clan, Banu Hashim, traditionally held the honour of Siqayah, supplying water to pilgrims who came to the Ka'bah.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the pre-Islamic Arab institution of 'Wa'd al-Banat'?
options: A dowry system favouring daughters over sons
The burying alive of infant daughters out of shame or fear of poverty
An annual festival honouring tribal mothers
A formal ceremony celebrating the birth of a daughter
questions.explanation: 'Wa'd al-Banat' refers to the practice of female infanticide in parts of pre-Islamic Arabia, a custom the Qur'an later condemned outright.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Before the rise of Islam, the Arabian Peninsula's northern borders were contested chiefly by which two rival empires?
options: The Byzantine (Roman) Empire and the Persian (Sassanid) Empire
The Chinese and the Indian empires
The Ottoman Empire and the Mongol Empire
The Egyptian and the Ethiopian kingdoms
questions.explanation: The Byzantines and Sassanid Persians vied for influence over the buffer Arab kingdoms on the fringes of Arabia, notably the Ghassanids and Lakhmids.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The pre-Islamic month during which fighting among Arab tribes was traditionally forbidden is referred to as
options: a market month
a pilgrimage recess
a month of mourning
a sacred (haram) month
questions.explanation: Certain months, known as the sacred months, were observed by pre-Islamic Arabs as periods in which warfare was traditionally prohibited, a custom Islam later retained.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Among the various religious communities present in pre-Islamic Arabia besides idol-worshippers were
options: Only strict atheists
Buddhists and Confucians
Followers of a single unified Arab church
Jews, Christians, and Hanifs who held to monotheism
questions.explanation: Alongside the dominant idolatry, pre-Islamic Arabia was also home to Jewish communities, Christian groups, and Hanifs, monotheists who rejected idol worship.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The pre-Islamic practice of 'Mut'ah' marriages and various irregular unions is significant to Tarikh mainly because
options: Islam abolished marriage altogether
such marriages were entirely unknown before Islam
Islam later reformed marriage practice by establishing clear conditions, rights, and responsibilities
these practices continued unchanged under Islamic law
questions.explanation: Pre-Islamic Arabia had a variety of loosely regulated marriage customs, which Islam later reformed by instituting clear contractual conditions and mutual rights.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The angel who brought divine revelation to Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W) is identified in Islamic teaching as
options: Israfil
Malik
Mika'il (Michael)
Jibril (Gabriel)
questions.explanation: Jibril is the angel entrusted by Allah with conveying revelation to the Prophets, including delivering the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Prior to receiving revelation, Prophet Muhammad was known to withdraw periodically to the Cave of Hira mainly to engage in
options: training for military campaigns
trade negotiations with Makkan merchants
quiet meditation and reflection
the writing of poetry for tribal contests
questions.explanation: Before prophethood, Muhammad regularly retreated to the solitude of the Cave of Hira for contemplation, away from the idolatry of Makkan society.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Among the earliest converts to Islam in Makkah, the first male adult to accept the faith is generally identified as
options: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab
Abu Bakr
'Uthman ibn 'Affan
'Ali ibn Abi Talib
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr is widely recognised as the first free adult male to accept Islam, becoming one of the Prophet's closest and most trusted companions.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The conversion of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab to Islam during the Makkan period is significant chiefly because it
options: led directly to the Hijrah the following week
resulted in 'Umar becoming the first Caliph
ended all opposition to Islam in Makkah immediately
gave the small Muslim community renewed strength and boldness to worship openly
questions.explanation: 'Umar's conversion, given his stature among the Quraysh, greatly emboldened the Muslims, who reportedly began to pray openly at the Ka'bah afterwards.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The economic boycott imposed on the clans of Banu Hashim and Banu Muttalib by the Makkan Quraysh was intended chiefly to
options: pressure the Prophet's protectors into abandoning their support for him
compel the migration of all Muslims to Abyssinia
force a permanent peace treaty with Madinah
punish the Quraysh's own trading partners
questions.explanation: The Quraysh imposed a social and economic boycott on the Prophet's clan in an effort to isolate and starve them into withdrawing their protection of him.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: During the Makkan period, the early Muslims' method of worship and gathering was chiefly characterised by
options: large public congregational events in the Ka'bah
state-sponsored ceremonies
open alliance with the Byzantine Empire
secrecy, due to the risk of persecution from the Quraysh
questions.explanation: For much of the early Makkan period, Muslims worshipped in secret and met discreetly to avoid the harsh persecution of the ruling Quraysh leaders.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The delegation from Yathrib (later Madinah) that pledged allegiance to the Prophet at 'Aqabah is remembered in Islamic history as agreeing chiefly to
options: finance the construction of a new Ka'bah
protect and support the Prophet if he migrated to their city
convert the Quraysh to Islam by force
supply Makkah with weapons against the Muslims
questions.explanation: The pledges of 'Aqabah were agreements by representatives of Yathrib to accept Islam and to protect and support the Prophet, paving the way for the Hijrah.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Bilal ibn Rabah is remembered in Islamic history chiefly for
options: enduring severe torture for his faith and later becoming the first muadhin (caller to prayer)
serving as the second Rightly Guided Caliph
leading the Muslim army at the Battle of Badr
compiling the Qur'an into a single written text
questions.explanation: Bilal, an Abyssinian companion, suffered brutal persecution for embracing Islam and was later honoured by the Prophet with the role of the first muadhin.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Quraysh's chief objections to Prophet Muhammad's message during the Makkan period centred mainly on his
options: rejection of idol worship and the ancestral religion of their forefathers
insistence that Makkah be relocated
call for the abolition of the Arabic language
demand that they pay increased trade taxes
questions.explanation: The Quraysh leadership fiercely resisted the Prophet's monotheistic call because it directly threatened their idol-based religious traditions and associated commercial interests.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The 'Year of the Elephant', traditionally cited as the year of the Prophet's birth, takes its name from
options: a famous battle fought entirely by elephant cavalry
a festival celebrating elephants sacred to the Quraysh
an aborted attack on the Ka'bah by Abrahah's army, which included war elephants
the arrival of Persian traders riding elephants
questions.explanation: The year is named for Abrahah's failed military expedition against the Ka'bah, an army that famously included elephants, an event described in Surah Al-Fil.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Prophet Muhammad's honorific title 'Al-Amin', earned before his prophethood, reflects his reputation among the Makkans for being
options: the wealthiest merchant in Makkah
trustworthy and honest
the most skilled warrior in Arabia
a famous poet of the 'Ukaz fair
questions.explanation: 'Al-Amin' means 'the trustworthy one', a title the Makkans gave Muhammad well before his prophethood due to his renowned honesty.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The event in which the Prophet was asked to settle a dispute among Quraysh clans over placing the Black Stone during the Ka'bah's reconstruction demonstrates chiefly his
options: role as head of a formal government
authority as a revealed prophet, since this occurred after revelation began
military leadership skill
wisdom and fairness in resolving conflict
questions.explanation: Before his prophethood, Muhammad was asked to arbitrate a dispute over the Black Stone and devised a fair solution using a cloth so every clan could share in carrying it, showcasing his wisdom.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The bond of brotherhood (Mu'akhah) established by the Prophet in Madinah paired each Muhajir (migrant) with
options: an Ansari (helper) from Madinah who shared resources and support
a Byzantine envoy
a Jewish tribal leader
a Quraysh chief from Makkah
questions.explanation: To integrate the migrants into their new community, the Prophet paired each Muhajir with an Ansari host, fostering deep mutual support and solidarity.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Under the terms of the Constitution of Madinah, the Jewish tribes residing in the city were generally guaranteed
options: complete exclusion from the city's affairs
religious freedom and a role in the collective defence of Madinah
forced conversion to Islam within one year
exemption from any obligation to the community
questions.explanation: The Constitution of Madinah recognised the Jewish tribes as part of the city's single political community, guaranteeing them religious liberty alongside shared defence obligations.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The primary reason the Muslims of Madinah engaged Makkan caravans, precipitating the Battle of Badr, was to
options: expand Islamic territory into Syria
avenge the death of Khadijah
seize control of the Ka'bah by force
recover losses suffered when their property was seized upon leaving Makkah
questions.explanation: Many Muhajirun had their property and wealth confiscated by the Quraysh when they emigrated, and the raids on Makkan trade caravans were partly aimed at redress.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: A key lesson Islamic scholars draw from the setback at the Battle of Uhud is the importance of
options: abandoning defensive positions once victory seems assured
strict obedience to the Prophet's military instructions
avoiding all warfare entirely
relying solely on numerical superiority in battle
questions.explanation: The Muslim setback at Uhud is widely attributed to a group of archers abandoning their assigned post against the Prophet's explicit instructions, underscoring the need for discipline.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The expulsion of the Banu Qaynuqa' from Madinah followed their
options: conversion to Christianity
violation of the Constitution of Madinah through hostile provocation
refusal to trade with Muslims
request to leave voluntarily for Syria
questions.explanation: The Banu Qaynuqa' were expelled after breaching the terms of the Constitution of Madinah through acts of hostility and provocation against the Muslim community.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Persian companion Salman al-Farisi is chiefly remembered in the Madinan period for
options: compiling the first written copy of the Qur'an
serving as the third Rightly Guided Caliph
suggesting the trench-digging strategy used at the Battle of the Trench
leading the conquest of Makkah
questions.explanation: Salman al-Farisi, drawing on Persian military practice unfamiliar to the Arabs, advised digging a trench around Madinah, a decisive tactic at the Battle of the Trench.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: One notable term of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah required the Muslims to
options: hand over the Ka'bah to Quraysh control forever
postpone their pilgrimage to Makkah that year and return the following year instead
pay an annual tribute to the Quraysh
permanently abandon the city of Madinah
questions.explanation: Among its terms, the treaty required the Muslims to turn back without performing pilgrimage that year, with permission granted to return and perform it the following year.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The immediate cause that led the Prophet to march on Makkah, resulting in its largely peaceful conquest, was
options: a formal declaration of war issued by the Quraysh
the death of Abu Sufyan
a request from the Byzantine Empire
a Quraysh-allied tribe's attack on an ally of the Muslims, breaching the Hudaybiyyah treaty
questions.explanation: The truce of Hudaybiyyah collapsed after a tribe allied with the Quraysh attacked an ally of the Muslims, giving the Prophet just cause to march on Makkah.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Upon the largely peaceful Conquest of Makkah, Prophet Muhammad's treatment of his former persecutors is best described as
options: confiscation of all Makkan property
mass execution of all Quraysh leaders
forced exile of the entire population
a general amnesty, forgiving even many of his former enemies
questions.explanation: Despite years of persecution, the Prophet largely granted a general pardon to the people of Makkah upon its conquest, a landmark act of clemency in Islamic history.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajjatul Wada'), performed by the Prophet shortly before his death, is significant mainly for
options: marking the founding of the city of Madinah
being the first pilgrimage ever performed by Muslims
the Farewell Sermon, which summarised core Islamic principles for the Ummah
the compilation of the entire Qur'an into one book
questions.explanation: During the Farewell Pilgrimage, the Prophet delivered his famous Farewell Sermon, addressing themes such as human equality, the sanctity of life and property, and women's rights.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Delegations (Wufud) that came to Madinah in large numbers toward the end of the Prophet's life mainly represented
options: foreign ambassadors seeking military alliances only
Quraysh leaders seeking to negotiate a new treaty
Jewish tribes requesting readmission to Madinah
various Arab tribes formally accepting Islam
questions.explanation: In what is known as the 'Year of Delegations', numerous tribes from across Arabia sent representatives to Madinah to formally embrace Islam, reflecting its rapid spread.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Prophet Muhammad's decision to appoint Usamah ibn Zayd, a young companion, to lead a military expedition shortly before his death illustrates his emphasis on
options: reliance solely on the Ansar for leadership roles
merit and capability over age in leadership
hereditary succession within his own family
excluding younger companions from responsibility
questions.explanation: By entrusting a significant command to the young Usamah ibn Zayd, the Prophet demonstrated that leadership should be based on ability rather than age or seniority.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Abu Bakr was selected as the first Caliph largely on the strength of his
options: closeness to the Prophet and the trust of the early community, evidenced at the gathering at Saqifah
status as the wealthiest man in Madinah
military conquest of Makkah
position as the Prophet's son-in-law
questions.explanation: Following debate at the Saqifah of Banu Sa'idah, the companions chose Abu Bakr as the first Caliph, largely due to his deep trust and closeness to the Prophet.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Ridda (apostasy) Wars during Abu Bakr's caliphate were fought chiefly to
options: resolve a succession dispute among the Prophet's companions
defend Madinah from a Quraysh invasion
expand Islamic rule into the Byzantine Empire
suppress tribes that renounced Islam or refused to pay Zakat after the Prophet's death
questions.explanation: After the Prophet's death, several tribes renounced Islam or refused to pay Zakat, prompting Abu Bakr to wage the Ridda Wars to restore the unity of the Ummah.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: One of the most significant achievements attributed to Abu Bakr's caliphate was the
options: establishment of the office of Qadi (judge)
conquest of Egypt
founding of the city of Baghdad
initial compilation of the scattered Qur'anic revelations into a single collected text
questions.explanation: Concerned by the loss of Qur'an reciters in battle, Abu Bakr, on 'Umar's advice, ordered Zayd ibn Thabit to gather the scattered revelations into a single compiled text.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The title 'Al-Farooq' (the one who distinguishes right from wrong), associated with the second Caliph, refers to
options: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab
'Ali ibn Abi Talib
'Uthman ibn 'Affan
Abu Bakr
questions.explanation: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was given the title 'Al-Farooq' for his renowned ability to clearly discern truth from falsehood and justice from injustice.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: During 'Umar's caliphate, the administrative innovation of establishing the Diwan (public register) was introduced chiefly to
options: record poetry composed at court
list the names of all Qur'an reciters
catalogue captured enemy weapons
organise the systematic distribution of state revenue and stipends among Muslims
questions.explanation: 'Umar established the Diwan as an administrative register to systematically manage and distribute state income, including stipends, to eligible Muslims.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Islamic (Hijri) calendar was formally instituted as the official dating system for the Muslim state during the caliphate of
options: Abu Bakr
'Uthman ibn 'Affan
'Ali ibn Abi Talib
'Umar ibn al-Khattab
questions.explanation: 'Umar formally adopted the Hijrah, the Prophet's migration to Madinah, as the starting point of the Islamic lunar calendar to standardise official dating.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: A defining achievement of 'Uthman ibn 'Affan's caliphate was his order to
options: standardise the Qur'anic text into a single authoritative version and distribute copies across the empire
relocate the capital permanently to Makkah
found the first Islamic university
abolish the office of Caliph
questions.explanation: Amid growing regional variation in recitation, 'Uthman commissioned a standard written copy of the Qur'an and had copies sent to the major Muslim provinces.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Growing discontent that eventually led to the assassination of 'Uthman ibn 'Affan was fuelled in part by accusations of
options: favouritism toward his own relatives in key administrative appointments
his abolition of the Zakat system
his rejection of the compiled Qur'an
his refusal to expand the Islamic empire
questions.explanation: Discontent grew among some Muslims who accused 'Uthman of nepotism in appointing relatives to influential governorships, contributing to the unrest that led to his assassination.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib's caliphate was significantly marked by internal conflict, most notably the
options: Ridda Wars against apostate tribes
Battle of Badr and the Battle of Uhud
Conquest of Makkah and the Farewell Pilgrimage
Battle of the Camel and the Battle of Siffin
questions.explanation: 'Ali's caliphate was dominated by civil strife within the Muslim community, notably the Battle of the Camel against 'A'ishah, Talhah and Zubayr, and the Battle of Siffin against Mu'awiyah.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The arbitration process following the Battle of Siffin ultimately contributed to the emergence of a dissenting group known as the
options: Muhajirun
Kharijites
Ahlul-Bayt
Ansar
questions.explanation: Dissatisfied with 'Ali's acceptance of arbitration after Siffin, a faction broke away and became known as the Kharijites, who later turned against both 'Ali and Mu'awiyah.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The period of the four Rightly Guided Caliphs (Khulafa' al-Rashidun) is generally regarded by Sunni scholars as significant chiefly because it
options: coincided with the founding of the Abbasid dynasty
saw the compilation of the six canonical Hadith books
was marked by uninterrupted peace and unity throughout
closely followed the precedent and example set by the Prophet in governance
questions.explanation: The Rightly Guided Caliphs are especially esteemed in Sunni tradition for governing in close accordance with the Prophet's precedent, despite the internal challenges they faced.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Under the early Rightly Guided Caliphs, rapid territorial expansion brought which two major empires into direct and sustained conflict with the Muslim state?
options: The Ethiopian Empire and the Roman Republic
The Ottoman Empire and the Mughal Empire
The Mongol Empire and the Chinese Empire
The Byzantine Empire and the Persian (Sassanid) Empire
questions.explanation: The swift expansion of the Islamic state under the Rightly Guided Caliphs led to major, sustained confrontations with both the Byzantine and Sassanid Persian Empires.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Islam is generally believed to have first spread into West Africa mainly through
options: European colonial missionaries
direct migration from Madinah
Arab and Berber traders travelling along trans-Saharan trade routes
military conquest by Ottoman armies
questions.explanation: Long before colonial rule, Islam entered West Africa gradually and largely peacefully through contact with Arab and Berber traders along established trans-Saharan trade routes.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Among the early West African empires, Islam gained particularly strong footing in the royal courts of
options: the Zulu Kingdom
the Kingdom of Great Zimbabwe
ancient Ghana, Mali, and Songhai
the Kingdom of Benin exclusively
questions.explanation: The great medieval West African empires of Ghana, Mali, and Songhai were key centres where Islam took root, particularly among ruling elites and merchant classes.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Mansa Musa, the famous fourteenth-century ruler of the Mali Empire, is especially remembered in Islamic history for his
options: lavish pilgrimage to Makkah, which showcased Mali's wealth to the wider Muslim world
leadership of the trans-Saharan slave trade
conquest of Madinah
role as one of the Rightly Guided Caliphs
questions.explanation: Mansa Musa's celebrated Hajj journey, marked by extraordinary displays of wealth, drew international attention to the Mali Empire and strengthened its Islamic and scholarly ties.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The West African city of Timbuktu became particularly renowned in Islamic scholarship for its
options: role as the seat of the Sokoto Caliphate
position as the capital of ancient Ghana
status as the first city to accept Islam in West Africa
centres of learning, notably the Sankore institution, and its manuscript tradition
questions.explanation: Timbuktu flourished as a major centre of Islamic learning, home to institutions such as Sankore and a vast tradition of preserved Arabic manuscripts.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Uthman Dan Fodio's nineteenth-century jihad in Hausaland was primarily directed against
options: Hausa rulers he accused of mixing Islam with un-Islamic customs and injustice
European colonial administrators
the Sultan of Morocco
the Mali Empire
questions.explanation: Uthman Dan Fodio launched his jihad against Hausa kings whom he accused of syncretism, corruption, and oppressive taxation contrary to Islamic teaching.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The political entity established following Uthman Dan Fodio's jihad, uniting much of Hausaland under Islamic rule, is known as the
options: Kanem-Bornu Empire
Mali Empire
Sokoto Caliphate
Songhai Empire
questions.explanation: The jihad culminated in the establishment of the Sokoto Caliphate, a major Islamic state that unified much of what is now northern Nigeria under a single caliph.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Uthman Dan Fodio's major written work, which set out his religious and reformist arguments, is titled
options: Al-Muqaddimah
Sahih al-Bukhari
Kitab al-Farq
Muwatta
questions.explanation: Among his numerous writings, 'Kitab al-Farq' ('The Book of Difference') was a key text in which Dan Fodio distinguished true Islamic governance from un-Islamic practice.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: After Uthman Dan Fodio, leadership of the Sokoto Caliphate's religious and administrative affairs was significantly carried forward by his son
options: Abdullahi dan Fodio
Muhammad Bello
Ahmadu Bello
Usman Bugaje
questions.explanation: Muhammad Bello, Dan Fodio's son, succeeded as Caliph and played a central role in consolidating and administering the Sokoto Caliphate after the jihad.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Nana Asma'u, the daughter of Uthman Dan Fodio, is especially celebrated in West African Islamic history for her
options: leadership of military campaigns against Kanem-Bornu
founding of the city of Timbuktu
role as the first Sultan of Sokoto
contributions to Islamic scholarship and the education of women
questions.explanation: Nana Asma'u was a prolific scholar and poet who played a major role in promoting Islamic education, particularly among women, within the Sokoto Caliphate.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The spread of Islam in West Africa is generally distinguished from its spread elsewhere by the fact that it occurred largely through
options: immediate and total imposition by conquering armies
peaceful trade and scholarship rather than military conquest, at least in its earliest stages
the direct efforts of the Rightly Guided Caliphs
European colonial enforcement
questions.explanation: In its earliest centuries, Islam's spread through West Africa was largely gradual and peaceful, carried mainly by traders, itinerant scholars, and clerics rather than conquest.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The resistance offered by some Hausa states, such as under Queen Amina's successors, to Uthman Dan Fodio's jihad reflected primarily their
options: alliance with European colonial powers
attachment to existing political authority and local customs alongside their own version of Islam
adherence to Christianity
outright rejection of Islam as a religion
questions.explanation: Resistance to the jihad often stemmed less from a rejection of Islam itself than from rulers' determination to preserve their political power and existing customary practices.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: One long-term effect of Uthman Dan Fodio's jihad on the spread of Islam in what is now Nigeria was that it
options: abolished the Arabic script in the region
ended the practice of Islam entirely in Hausaland
led to the conversion of southern Nigeria to Islam
deepened and consolidated Islamic practice and learning across much of the north
questions.explanation: The jihad and the resulting Sokoto Caliphate greatly strengthened and standardised Islamic religious practice, education, and governance across much of northern Nigeria.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The term used for the gradual, piecemeal manner in which the Qur'an was revealed over approximately 23 years is
options: Tajweed
Tanjeem (revelation in stages)
Tafsir
Isnad
questions.explanation: Unlike scriptures revealed all at once, the Qur'an was revealed gradually over roughly 23 years, a process referred to as Tanjeem, suited to guiding the community as events unfolded.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The night on which the first revelation of the Qur'an is believed to have descended is commemorated in Islam as
options: Laylatul Mi'raj
Laylatul Bara'ah
Laylatul Qadr (the Night of Power/Decree)
Laylatul Hijrah
questions.explanation: Laylatul Qadr, occurring during Ramadan, is honoured as the blessed night on which the Qur'an's revelation began, described in the Qur'an itself as better than a thousand months.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Chapters of the Qur'an revealed before the Hijrah are generally classified as
options: Madinan Surahs
Makkan Surahs
Hijazi Surahs
Rashidun Surahs
questions.explanation: Surahs revealed before the Prophet's migration to Madinah are classified as Makkan, typically shorter and focused on core beliefs such as Tawhid and the Hereafter.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Surahs revealed after the Hijrah, generally dealing with legislation and community affairs, are classified as
options: Meccan Ayat
Madinan Surahs
Hanifi Surahs
Makkan Surahs
questions.explanation: Madinan Surahs, revealed after the migration, tend to be longer and address legal, social, and communal matters relevant to the growing Muslim state.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: In the earliest period, the primary method by which the Qur'an was preserved, alongside writing, was through
options: memorisation by the Prophet and his companions
translation into Aramaic
encoding in poetic verse for public recital contests
storage in the Ka'bah archives
questions.explanation: Memorisation played a central role in preserving the Qur'an from the outset, with the Prophet and numerous companions committing the revelations to heart as they were revealed.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The companion primarily entrusted by Abu Bakr with compiling the scattered Qur'anic material into a single text was
options: Bilal ibn Rabah
Zayd ibn Thabit
Salman al-Farisi
Khalid ibn al-Walid
questions.explanation: Zayd ibn Thabit, one of the Prophet's scribes, was chosen for his diligence and knowledge to carry out the careful task of compiling the Qur'an.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The impetus for Abu Bakr's compilation of the Qur'an arose largely from concern following the
options: death of many Qur'an reciters (Huffaz) at the Battle of Yamamah
loss of the original revelation in a fire
dispute among the Rightly Guided Caliphs over doctrine
request of the Byzantine emperor
questions.explanation: The deaths of numerous Huffaz during the Battle of Yamamah alarmed the companions, prompting 'Umar to urge Abu Bakr to have the Qur'an formally compiled.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: 'Uthman's standardisation of the Qur'an addressed a growing concern over
options: variations in recitation and dialect that risked causing disunity among Muslims
the physical loss of all existing copies of the Qur'an
the translation of the Qur'an into foreign languages
disagreement over the number of prophets mentioned in the text
questions.explanation: As Islam spread across diverse regions, differing recitation traditions began to cause disputes, prompting 'Uthman to establish and circulate one standard written text.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The system of diacritical marks and dots later added to the Qur'anic text was primarily intended to
options: assist non-Arab reciters in reading the text accurately
translate the Qur'an into Persian
indicate the chronological order of revelation
replace the need for memorisation entirely
questions.explanation: As Islam spread to non-Arabic speakers, diacritical marks were introduced to the originally undotted script to help ensure accurate pronunciation and reading.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Qur'an describes itself, in terms of its own preservation, as being safeguarded through
options: annual renewal ceremonies at the Ka'bah
the exclusive efforts of the Umayyad Caliphs
translation into every world language
Allah's own guarantee to protect it from corruption
questions.explanation: The Qur'an asserts in Surah Al-Hijr that Allah Himself has undertaken to preserve the text from alteration or loss.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Surah Al-Fatihah, recited in every unit (rak'ah) of the five daily prayers, is often referred to as
options: the Chapter of Cattle
the Chapter of Light
the Chapter of Repentance
the Opening (or 'the essence of the Qur'an')
questions.explanation: Al-Fatihah, meaning 'the Opening', is the first chapter of the Qur'an and is regarded as summarising its central themes, recited in every unit of the formal prayer.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Surah Al-Ikhlas is especially notable in Islamic teaching for its concise and direct affirmation of
options: the absolute oneness (Tawhid) of Allah
the story of Prophet Yusuf
the details of the Farewell Pilgrimage
the rules of inheritance
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ikhlas succinctly affirms Allah's absolute oneness, stating that He is neither begotten nor begets, and that nothing is comparable to Him.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Surah Al-Kahf is traditionally recommended for recitation especially on
options: the Day of 'Arafah
the tenth of Muharram
Fridays
the first night of Ramadan
questions.explanation: Prophetic tradition encourages the regular recitation of Surah Al-Kahf on Fridays, and it contains several instructive parables, including that of the People of the Cave.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Surah Yasin is often described by Muslim scholars as occupying a place of special reverence, sometimes referred to as
options: 'the seal of the prophets'
'the heart of the Qur'an'
'the mother of battles'
'the treaty of the believers'
questions.explanation: Surah Yasin is widely regarded among Muslims as holding a central and highly esteemed place within the Qur'an, often described as its 'heart'.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Surah Al-Baqarah, the longest chapter of the Qur'an, contains the well-known Ayatul Kursi, a verse especially notable for describing
options: the story of the Farewell Sermon
the rules of fasting in Ramadan
the details of the Hijrah
the majesty, knowledge, and sovereignty of Allah
questions.explanation: Ayatul Kursi, found in Surah Al-Baqarah, is renowned for its powerful description of Allah's supreme knowledge, sovereignty, and majesty.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Surah Al-'Asr, though brief, is regarded by many scholars as summarising the entire message of the Qur'an regarding
options: the specific rules of trade contracts
the necessity of faith, righteous deeds, and mutual counsel to avoid loss
the historical account of the Rightly Guided Caliphs
the geography of pre-Islamic Arabia
questions.explanation: Despite its brevity, Surah Al-'Asr is considered by scholars such as Ash-Shafi'i to encapsulate the essential path to avoiding loss: faith, good deeds, and mutual reminders of truth and patience.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Surah Al-Fil recounts the historical episode of
options: the compilation of the Qur'an by 'Uthman
Abrahah's failed attack on the Ka'bah using war elephants
the conquest of Makkah
the migration of the Prophet to Madinah
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Fil narrates the destruction of Abrahah's army, which had marched on the Ka'bah with elephants, an event tied to the Prophet's birth year.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Surah Al-Masad is notable in Tarikh for its direct and explicit condemnation of
options: the Persian emperor Khosrow
Abu Lahab and his wife for their hostility to the Prophet
the Byzantine emperor Heraclius
the Quraysh as a whole without naming individuals
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Masad is unusual among Qur'anic chapters for explicitly naming and condemning Abu Lahab and his wife for their relentless opposition to the Prophet.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: A Hadith, in Islamic terminology, refers primarily to
options: a ruling issued exclusively by a Caliph
a report of the sayings, actions, or approvals of Prophet Muhammad
a poem composed in praise of the Prophet
any verse of the Qur'an
questions.explanation: Hadith literature comprises reports recording what the Prophet said, did, or tacitly approved, forming a foundational source of Islamic teaching alongside the Qur'an.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The chain of narrators through which a Hadith is transmitted back to the Prophet is technically known as the
options: Matn
Isnad (or sanad)
Tafsir
Ijma'
questions.explanation: The Isnad is the chain of transmitters cited before the text of a Hadith, and its scrutiny is central to assessing the report's authenticity.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The actual wording or textual content of a Hadith report, as distinct from its chain of narrators, is termed the
options: Qiyas
Matn
Isnad
Ijtihad
questions.explanation: The Matn refers specifically to the substantive text or content of a Hadith, which scholars examine alongside the Isnad in assessing authenticity.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: A Hadith graded 'Sahih' by Muslim scholars of Hadith criticism is one judged to be
options: definitely fabricated
authentic, having met the strict criteria of a sound, unbroken, and reliable chain of narration
narrated only through a single companion with no other corroboration permitted
of uncertain or weak reliability
questions.explanation: 'Sahih' denotes the highest grade of authenticity, assigned to Hadiths whose chain of transmission and content satisfy rigorous scholarly criteria.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Among the six canonical Hadith collections widely accepted by Sunni Muslims, the two most authoritative are generally considered to be those compiled by
options: Imam Bukhari and Imam Muslim
Imam Malik and Imam Shafi'i
Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Hisham
Imam Abu Hanifah and Imam Ahmad
questions.explanation: The collections of Imam Bukhari (Sahih al-Bukhari) and Imam Muslim (Sahih Muslim) are traditionally regarded as the most authoritative among the six canonical Hadith books.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Imam Malik's compilation of Hadith and legal rulings, notable for reflecting the practice of the people of Madinah, is titled
options: Al-Muwatta
Sunan Abu Dawud
Sahih al-Bukhari
Musnad Ahmad
questions.explanation: Al-Muwatta, compiled by Imam Malik ibn Anas, blends Hadith with the legal practice of Madinah and is among the earliest major works of Islamic law and Hadith.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The compilers of Hadith developed a rigorous discipline for scrutinising narrators' reliability and character mainly to
options: translate Hadith texts into other languages
determine the order of Surahs in the Qur'an
safeguard the authenticity of reports attributed to the Prophet
compile the Qur'an into a single text
questions.explanation: Given the religious weight attached to Prophetic reports, scholars developed strict criteria for evaluating narrators to protect against fabrication or error.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: A Hadith is classified as 'Da'if' (weak) primarily when its chain of narration or content
options: contradicts pre-Islamic Arab poetry
was narrated exclusively by the Prophet's own family
was recorded after the compilation of the Qur'an
fails to meet the criteria required for a sound or authentic classification
questions.explanation: A Da'if Hadith is one whose chain of transmission or textual content contains weaknesses that prevent it from meeting the criteria of Sahih or Hasan grading.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Islamic doctrine of Tawhid refers fundamentally to belief in
options: the equal status of all the prophets
the political unity of the Muslim Ummah
the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah
the unity of all world religions
questions.explanation: Tawhid is the foundational Islamic doctrine affirming that Allah is one, without partners, equals, or division, in His essence, attributes, and worship.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The aspect of Tawhid concerned specifically with Allah's exclusive right to be worshipped is known as
options: Tawhid al-Asma' wa-Sifat
Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah
Tawhid al-Hakimiyyah only
Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah
questions.explanation: Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah, or the oneness of worship, affirms that acts of worship must be directed to Allah alone, without associating any partner with Him.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The aspect of Tawhid affirming Allah as the sole Creator, Sustainer, and Controller of the universe is termed
options: Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah
Tawhid al-Ibadah only
Tawhid al-Hakimiyyah exclusively
Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah
questions.explanation: Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah affirms Allah's oneness in creating, sustaining, and governing all that exists, a belief acknowledged even by many pre-Islamic Arabs.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Shirk, as understood in Islamic theology, refers to
options: failure to perform the five daily prayers
any minor sin committed unintentionally
associating partners with Allah in His divinity or worship
disbelief in the finality of prophethood alone
questions.explanation: Shirk is the gravest sin in Islam, involving the association of partners with Allah, whether in worship, attributes, or divine authority.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Which of the following is generally classified by Islamic scholars as an example of major Shirk?
options: Making a minor error in prayer recitation
Directing acts of worship, such as prayer or sacrifice, to someone or something other than Allah
Showing off slightly while doing a good deed
Performing an act of worship with slight distraction
questions.explanation: Major Shirk involves openly directing core acts of worship, such as prayer, supplication, or sacrifice, to something other than Allah, which nullifies one's faith.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The concept of 'Riya' (ostentation), performing good deeds to be seen and praised by others, is generally classified by scholars as
options: an obligatory act of worship
a form of minor Shirk
a pillar of Iman
a recommended act of charity
questions.explanation: Riya, or performing acts of worship for the sake of being seen and praised rather than sincerely for Allah, is regarded by scholars as a form of minor Shirk.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Islamic concept of Al-Asma' wal-Sifat concerns belief in
options: the ninety-nine names of the Prophet's companions
the titles given to the Rightly Guided Caliphs
the names attributed to angels only
Allah's beautiful names and attributes as described in revelation, without distortion or resemblance to creation
questions.explanation: Tawhid al-Asma' wal-Sifat concerns affirming Allah's names and attributes exactly as revealed, without distorting their meaning or likening them to created beings.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The declaration of faith, 'La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur Rasulullah', is central to Tawhid because it affirms both
options: the unity of the four Rightly Guided Caliphs
the oneness of Allah and the prophethood of Muhammad
the five pillars of Islam in full
the finality of the Qur'an's compilation
questions.explanation: The Shahadah simultaneously affirms Allah's exclusive oneness and Prophet Muhammad's role as His final messenger, forming the very foundation of Islamic belief.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The five daily prayers (Salat) are generally regarded in Islamic teaching as
options: an optional act recommended only during Ramadan
an obligatory pillar of Islam prescribed for every sane, adult Muslim
required only of those who have performed Hajj
obligatory for men but merely encouraged for women
questions.explanation: Salat is one of the five pillars of Islam, obligatory upon every sane adult Muslim, forming a direct and regular act of worship and connection with Allah.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Zakat, as an obligatory form of worship, is best described as
options: a tax paid exclusively by non-Muslims
a fee paid only during the Hajj season
a prescribed portion of qualifying wealth given annually to specified categories of recipients
a voluntary donation given at any time of one's choosing
questions.explanation: Zakat is a fixed, obligatory portion of a Muslim's qualifying wealth, distributed annually to specified categories of recipients as outlined in the Qur'an.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The fast of Ramadan (Sawm) obligates a Muslim to abstain, from dawn until sunset, chiefly from
options: speaking to other people entirely
food, drink, and other invalidating acts
reading the Qur'an aloud
leaving one's home for any reason
questions.explanation: Fasting in Ramadan requires abstention from food, drink, and other acts that invalidate the fast, from dawn until sunset, as an act of worship and self-discipline.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The pilgrimage to Makkah (Hajj) becomes obligatory upon a Muslim under which of the following conditions?
options: Every year, for every adult Muslim without exception
Only for those born in Arabia
Once in a lifetime, for those who are physically and financially able
Only for scholars of Islamic law
questions.explanation: Hajj is obligatory only once in a lifetime, and only upon Muslims who possess the physical capability and financial means to undertake the journey.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The ritual of Sa'i, performed during Hajj and 'Umrah, commemorates
options: the Prophet's flight from Makkah to Madinah
the sacrifice of Prophet Ibrahim's ram
Hajar's search for water between the hills of Safa and Marwah
the stoning of Satan at Mina
questions.explanation: Sa'i re-enacts Hajar's desperate search for water for her infant son Isma'il, running between the hills of Safa and Marwah, an episode central to Hajj rites.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The ritual of stoning the pillars (Rami al-Jamarat) during Hajj is understood to symbolise
options: the punishment of the Quraysh for persecuting the Prophet
the rejection of Satan's temptations, following the example of Prophet Ibrahim
the destruction of idols at the Ka'bah
the defeat of the Makkan army at Badr
questions.explanation: Rami al-Jamarat commemorates Prophet Ibrahim's rejection of Satan's attempts to dissuade him from obeying Allah's command, symbolising the pilgrim's own rejection of evil.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The term 'Shariah' in Islamic usage refers broadly to
options: the comprehensive body of Islamic law derived from the Qur'an and Sunnah
the historical record of the Rightly Guided Caliphs
only the criminal punishments prescribed in Islam
a specific book of Hadith
questions.explanation: Shariah denotes the broad framework of Islamic law and guidance, covering worship, ethics, and social conduct, derived primarily from the Qur'an and Sunnah.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: In Islamic jurisprudence, 'Mu'amalat' refers specifically to matters concerning
options: social and commercial transactions between people, such as contracts and trade
the biography of the Prophet
the rituals of worship alone
the study of Qur'anic recitation rules
questions.explanation: Mu'amalat covers the branch of Islamic law dealing with interpersonal social and commercial dealings, including contracts, trade, and financial transactions.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Riba (usury/interest) is treated in Islamic commercial law as
options: strictly prohibited, regardless of the rate charged
encouraged in trade between Muslims and non-Muslims
permissible only in transactions involving gold
permissible provided the rate is reasonably low
questions.explanation: Islamic law categorically prohibits Riba in commercial and financial dealings, viewing it as exploitative and contrary to principles of fairness in trade.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: A valid contract of sale (Bay') in Islamic commercial law generally requires
options: mutual consent of both parties and clarity regarding the subject matter and price
that goods only be exchanged for gold
that the transaction take place inside a mosque
the involvement of a government official as witness in every case
questions.explanation: For a sale to be valid under Islamic commercial law, both parties must freely consent, and the item and price involved must be clearly known to avoid uncertainty (Gharar).
